core_principles.text: Start the bicep curl with the elbow in full extension and the forearm supinated.
Stand against a wall with the opposite arm placed behind the back to prevent excessive body movement.
Inspire throughout the eccentric phase and expire throughout the concentric phase to maintain a constant breathing rate.

common_mistakes.text: Allowing excessive body movement to assist in lifting the dumbbell.
Failing to start the movement with the elbow in full extension.

specific_findings.text: The study utilized a repetition timing of 2 seconds concentric and 2 seconds eccentric monitored by a metronome.
To minimize the effect of changing abdominal pressures, participants maintained a constant breathing rate of 15 breaths per minute.
Failure during 1-RM testing was defined as the final load successfully lifted with correct technique where an additional 0.5 kg could not be lifted.

consequences.text: Performing a Valsalva maneuver during bicep curls can alter abdominal pressure, which affects cardiac output and blood pressure.
